items.name: Aikido 'Altar'
items.summary: Belgian cybersecurity firm Aikido released 'Altar', an open-weight AI model built for security use cases that teams can run locally instead of sending sensitive code to external providers. It is a compressed, customized version of Z.AI's open GLM-5.3 model and is already being deployed in Aikido's customer solutions.

items.name: CYDELPHI CYVISIONARY
items.summary: CYDELPHI unveiled CYVISIONARY, billed as the industry's first AI-native digital forensics and incident response (DFIR) platform, using AI and agentic workflows to automate breach preparation, response and recovery — aiming to restore critical operations in hours instead of weeks.

items.name: Axoflow AxoDetect
items.summary: Axoflow launched AxoDetect (early access), which runs Sigma detection rules directly in the telemetry pipeline on normalized data — alerts travel to the SIEM while full-fidelity logs land in its low-cost AxoLake data lake, cutting SIEM ingest costs by half or more in early deployments.

items.name: SARAAB (DESC)
items.summary: The Dubai Electronic Security Center unveiled SARAAB, an open-source AI model built by an Emirati team to detect deepfake videos — the first of its kind from a government entity in the Arab region — and will publish it on developer platforms for researchers to test and extend.

items.name: DigiCert AI Trust Manager
items.summary: DigiCert launched AI Trust Manager (general availability) on its DigiCert ONE platform to discover and govern enterprise AI agents — giving each agent a cryptographically signed 'AI Passport' identity, policy-based 'visas' defining what it may access, and a kill switch to revoke authority when trust changes.
